subject: UX defect: stale digest banner is alarming and uninformative
body:
Leader issue: `the record has moved since this page was drawn` appears as a warning on every page and looks like an error.

What I verified:
- It is not a runtime error; the digest did change when I assigned work and wrote messages.
- `/api/state` and `/api/digest` currently agree, so after a reload the banner clears.
- The banner is global in App.vue, so every pane shows it even when the record change is only a new outbox message/task.
- It says nothing about what changed or what to do.

Please own this UX defect:
1. Do not render this as a red/warning error; it is a normal collaboration event.
2. Move it to a subtle status affordance in the header (for example a badge/quiet button), not a large alert on every page.
3. Say something human and actionable: `New records are available` + `Load updates`, and preserve scroll/thread position.
4. Do not auto-force reload while a person is reading or typing.
5. If feasible, describe the changed scope from the digest endpoint (conversation/task/plan), but do not fabricate a count if it is unavailable.
6. Add an E2E test that changes state after first render, asserts the quiet affordance appears, clicking it loads the new state, scroll position/selection is preserved, and no full-page navigation occurs.

This is part of the same dashboard dogfooding batch.
